nodes.title: Run actionlint as a declared Bazel test
nodes.summary:
The original actionlint change is fully replaced by merged import #15250 at d3f4faffa. Upstream deliberately made the Bazel actions check optional, so default lint no longer requires host Bazel. The old default-lint failure is resolved. The Make-wrapper follow-up at 8f772e58b is retired as an unnecessary request; its source, validation refs and original failed-parent evidence are preserved. It was not landed. Complete six-path replacement review and independent peer 493c0a58dbdf closed; normal exact-lease remote deletion and named local deletion are verified (receipt bffaa781a15c). Only bazel-actionlint was retired; bazel-actionlint-ci remains preserved.

The reviewed actionlint correction is integrated in public, clean and tracked MAIN 1670b46d8ba7725ee2b3c7619951e216ba53ce00. Validation continuation 3f824ddf-8b12-40b3-ae4f-8f27fc12bb63 at unchanged fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 runs both selected test paths uncached: the canonical Docker-builder test passes in 20 ms, and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false passes through RBE in 98 ms. Default evidence is the actual BEP/result output without materialized XML; the RBE result has its actual Action/Command/worker/log/XML join. Sealed outcome e6382a9238e1 retains the parent FAILED after 78.680 seconds solely because default-builder shutdown returns 2; both test phases and captures succeed, and final cleanup returns zero. That contributor request is now retired because the landed optional-check contract resolves its motivating default-lint failure. This does not claim a complete public import or full-CI pass.

The authorized October 2/3 rebase is published at e89cc398592a9e40b0d876bba1d2052e045d2314 on current master b65c70734a1bc7df49d000b911848b3ad2a9cce0. The requested attributed comment to @EtiennePerot is verified at https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/15107#issuecomment-5963408537. Current checks and feedback are recorded in the GitHub snapshot; mergeability does not establish review or CI completion. Public older-source import #15250 at 263162ee3de76a03c0cd68da9f2eba16373201fe fails Buildkite 49348: the host lint step reports that Bazel is absent from PATH. The import contains older source 6db816c6c, while the live source PR remains e89cc3985. The owning correction delegates the actions check through canonical make test, preserving the default builder route and explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false. Its narrow source/record peer passed; the proposed wrapper is preserved as historical evidence. This failure does not establish that the unrelated Podman result has the same cause. The first hosted correction validation at fork source 8f772e58b6981a9e4c8da4acedebb2b89d1812b0 fails after 1,234.198 seconds (parent 65a1d557-984f-446c-a969-4818964d9ee3, sealed outcome 33eab553e459). The canonical builder image pull and container startup succeed, and Make reaches its TEST header; no actual Bazel test result is captured before the deadline and exit 137. The explicit DOCKER_BUILD=false phase never executes. Noninteractive post-timeout inspection can run Bazel 8.3.1 in the still-running builder. Cause is unproved; the later method-only continuation removes inherited terminal input and gives collection a separate bounded deadline. The coordinator reports Linux 5.15, distinct from the observed Linux 6.1 action workers; neither is evidence of a newer worker deployment. The original public import failure and this incomplete validation remain separate.

followup.nextAction: No follow-up is requested. Preserve the reviewed optional-wrapper source and historical validation evidence.

nodes.title: Support external buffer storage
nodes.summary:
Public buffer-external-storage-refresh@1c636c974ff648d8e67fffb6280e01599e117bf5 is an independent refresh on verified upstream e1bc74024. Complete source/record peer 1ab800726bc5 and immutable binding 16ec469922b0 verify the reviewed seven-path patch and final message; original d065 remains preserved. External chunks use existing references, release exactly once, detach shared writes to heap storage and preserve owner sharing through checkpoint restoration without accessing unready storage. Concrete owners must restore accessible bytes before use. This adds no MemoryFile owner or TUN write-policy change. The clone-growth prerequisite and populated benchmark correction are already upstream.

The owning implementation and benchmarks match historically tested composition 4f81, apart from two test contexts and a comment explaining the existing size bound. Recovered primary parent 46357 is OK in 95.090 seconds, with the complete buffer owner, benchmark owner and both owning Nogo targets passing; parent console confirms both CPU analyses and five candidate samples per benchmark. The earlier 326-entry XML and authentic COW failure remain attributed to the closed prior record, not newly recovered leaf artifacts. Recorded medians rise from 3.924 to 4.535 ns for ReadAt (+15.6%) and 64.30 to 66.31 ns for WriteRead (+3.1%), with zero allocations. Worker identity is unknown; these are possible costs, not a statistical or causal performance claim. No fresh current-master, ARM runtime, real asynchronous packet restore or oversized TUN parity result is claimed.

The contributor answered the 066a review request by asking for the missing TUN context. The message-only revision is now published at a971becd35c244f8a93c16b91ee544be16e02bd5, explaining Linux writes beyond the MTU, current Go-heap allocation, and why a later MemoryFile-backed TUN change needs this buffer lifetime support. Independent editorial and factual review passed; the source tree and validation evidence are unchanged. The contributor then approved publication subject to comment corrections. Exact amendment 1c636 clarifies disjoint heap/external storage and moves Bytes/Release requirements onto their methods; noncomment bytes and the reviewed message are unchanged (independent peer 804528225dfe). Ready PR #15443 is now open against master, with verified body, head, tracking and thread metadata. CI and review are being followed by the standing sweep.
